prompt:
Write a police officer's crash report narrative (about 150 words). Collision type: side impact at intersection in Houston, Texas. The claimant was a driver and reported shoulder injury. Refer to people as Driver 1, Driver 2 or Passenger. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1372; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- It is not clear whether all of the damage came from this impact.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text: Officer's narrative: On arrival at the signalized intersection in Houston, Texas, I found a side-impact collision between two passenger vehicles in the eastbound and northbound lanes. Driver 1 was seated behind the wheel of the eastbound vehicle and reported pain in the right shoulder, which I observed was consistent with the direction and force of the impact to the driver's side. Driver 2 operated the northbound vehicle and stated that the collision occurred as Driver 1 described it. Two independent witnesses on the sidewalk gave statements that matched both drivers' accounts, and scene photographs taken at my request show the same sequence of contact. A Passenger was also present in the eastbound vehicle, and both officers on scene and the witnesses confirmed that person was inside at the time. Driver 1 is listed as the named insured on the vehicle's policy. I found no indication of prior damage to either vehicle. The extent of the damage to the eastbound vehicle's rear quarter panel is not clearly attributable to this impact alone and will require further inspection.
